title: Octanol-treated worms show more isopotential regions, which return to normal by 30 days

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Octanol-treated worms show more isopotential regions, which return to normal by 30 days

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Ten days after transient octanol exposure, regenerated G. dorotocephala show more distinct isopotential (membrane-voltage) regions by DiBAC dye imaging than controls, and the number of isopotential regions returns to the wild-type level after 30 days of morphological remodeling.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 2. Results › 2.6. Patterns of Endogenous Relative Membrane Potential Are Altered in GJ-Perturbed Worms

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We detected an increased number of isopotential regions in the pseudo worms compared to the states of control worms; interestingly, the numbers of isopotential regions return to those of a wild-type state after 30 days of morphological remodeling (Figure 6I).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M, Durant F, Hammelman J, Bessonov N, Volpert V, Morokuma J, Pinet K, Adams DS, Pietak A, Lobo D, Levin M, “Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms”, International journal of molecular sciences (2015), doi:10.3390/ijms161126065; section “2. Results › 2.6. Patterns of Endogenous Relative Membrane Potential Are Altered in GJ-Perturbed Worms”. Scope: Whole-body DiBAC4(3) voltage-dye images of octanol-treated and control G. dorotocephala at 10 and 30 days

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-girardia-06: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The temporal comparison and image-analysis criterion are explicit, but only published images and summaries are clearly public. Dye and segmentation limitations also weaken discrimination between connectivity changes and imaging artifacts.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reprocess day-10 and day-30 DiBAC images with a fixed segmentation pipeline and compare the number of isopotential regions among treated and control worms. Support requires an excess at day 10 and convergence to control values at day 30.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
DiBAC intensity is relative and sensitive to penetration and segmentation choices.

The full raw image stack is not clearly deposited.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.55
analysis feasibility: 0.75
operationalizability: 0.9
data adequacy: 0.45
data existence: 0.5

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The region-count procedure is specified well enough to repeat on images, including the cluster count and size filter. Those images and the animal-level counts are not in a public archive. Re-reading the summary figure cannot replace that reanalysis, so the time course still needs the raw recordings or a new imaging series.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Apply the paper's five-cluster segmentation to flat-fielded DiBAC images and compare isopotential-region counts at day 10 and day 30 between octanol-treated and control worms. More regions at day 10 and a return to control counts at day 30 would support the time course; no difference, or no return, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Raw DiBAC images and per-animal region counts are not public.

The count depends on a five-cluster threshold and a 15-pixel size filter.

fields.label: Dimension scores
